newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 81 -1 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 146 +1 on last week

AMLC COMMENTARY: A general drying in weather conditions across Australia has tightened feed supplies and forced increasing numbers of unfinished livestock into saleyards and direct to works in the first weeks of January.

Processors have taken advantage of the increasing in offerings and are currently killing at rates above those of last year. Cattle slaughter in Queensland last week was 26,000 head compared with 20,500 in the same week last year, whilst in New South Wales kills were up by 3,000 head on the same week last year. If current weather patterns persist, it would be no
surprise to see kills remaining well above year ago levels.
In contrast to weather conditions across Australia, extremely cold conditions in the northern hemisphere are disrupting markets, especially in the U.S.

Average carcass weights are currently around four percent below a year ago. Although U.S. numbers on feed remain three percent above one year ago levels, these lower carcass weights will have a moderating affect on U.S. production.
In Japan the beef market, wholesale prices for chilled product have remained stable compared to pre-Christmas levels.
Grassfed fullsets are trading at 645Y/kg whilst shortfed fullsets are 780Y/kg.

Export prices to Japan have remained steady on pre-Christmas rates. Tight supplies rather than strong consumer demand seems to be holding prices as, generally, demand for beef in Japan during January and February is subdued.
A positive development since the Christmas break has been the continued depreciation of the Australian dollar.

Since reaching $US.81 in late November the dollar has fallen to around $US.78. This decline has been sparked by speculation of higher interest rates in the US and lower interest rates in Australia. A lower Australian dollar will assist in strengthening export returns and increasing Australia's competitiveness.
